title: Sliding Networks: A Family of Residual Structures Preserving Feature Learning and Feature Diversity
abstract: Deep learning models tend to perform best at large widths and depths. The growing interest in scaling laws, especially in the language modeling domain, has motivated procedures for scaling up network widths and depths in order to preserve stability and computational efficiency of training dynamics. Existing depth-scaling approaches force a choice between retaining locally maximal \emph{feature learning} and preserving a form of \emph{feature diversity} in the residual stream arising from random differences between channels. We examine a \textit{joint scaling recipe} that preserves both. With residual width $N_\flat$, hidden width $N_\sharp$, and depth $L$, the key quantity is, by default, the limiting ratio $N_\flat/(N_\sharp L)\toα$, while correlated initialization (Half Copy) can partially relax the resulting shape constraints. Theory and residual-MLP experiments support convergence at fixed positive $α$ to an SDE limit with locally maximal feature learning. Hidden computations can then be redistributed between width and depth while preserving this limit, like turning melody into harmony and back. Language-model experiments nevertheless show performance differences under regrouping at fixed parameter count. These results distinguish approximating a limit (ODE or SDE) from scaling for better performance.
summary: This paper introduces a joint scaling recipe for deep neural networks that resolves the tension between maximizing feature learning and maintaining feature diversity as models scale. By deriving continuous-depth limits, the authors show that computations can be flexibly redistributed between network width and depth while preserving performance. This work provides a powerful theoretical tool for understanding the scaling laws governing modern AI architectures.
main_problem: The paper addresses how to design a joint scaling recipe for deep neural networks that simultaneously preserves both local feature learning capacity and feature diversity as model size increases.
main_result: A joint scaling recipe, particularly in the Stochastic Differential Equation (SDE) limit, was shown to preserve both feature learning and diversity, allowing computations to be 'slid' between width and depth while maintaining performance.
method: The authors use theoretical analysis, deriving continuous-depth limits (SDE/ODE) for residual MLP structures, complemented by empirical testing on language modeling tasks.
model_or_system: The model analyzed is a residual MLP structure, analogous to Transformer blocks, where the dynamics are tracked across residual ($\mathbf{h}_ lat$) and hidden ($\mathbf{h}_\sharp$) activation streams.
key_observables: Residual width ($N_{	ext{res}}$), hidden width ($N_{	ext{hid}}$), depth ($L$), the scaling ratio $\alpha = N_{	ext{res}}/(N_{	ext{hid}}L)$, and energy components ($E_0, Q, C$).
important_parameters: The scaling ratio $\alpha$, the effective learning rate ceiling ($\eta_{	ext{eff,max}}$), and the number of training updates/tokens.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that the network dynamics can be accurately approximated by continuous limits (ODE or SDE) and that the MLP residual structure is a sufficient model for understanding scaling laws.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the standard residual MLP structure, the evolution of residual coordinates through depth (GPT-2 activations), and convergence of kernel errors versus depth/updates.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from defining the scaling challenge (feature learning vs. diversity) to deriving theoretical limits (SDE/ODE) for the residual MLP, demonstrating the 'sliding' mechanism, and finally validating these concepts with large-scale language model experiments.
why_interesting: The mathematical framework used to analyze the stability and scaling of deep neural networks shares conceptual parallels with analyzing complex, high-dimensional physical systems, such as those modeled by disordered Hamiltonians or in the context of quantum information flow.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
